Dodge Charger SRT Hellcat Races R35 Nissan GT-R, Someone Wins the Fight By Just One Mile Per Hour
14 photos
Photo: Import 2 Race / YouTube
Once again, we have been waiting in vain: it’s already been a decidedly long time since the good folks over at the racing-focused ' Import 2 Race ' channel on YouTube have not yet returned to their traditional venue - Island Dragway in Great Meadows, New Jersey. Instead, they’re still into roll races.
Instead of feisty quarter-mile dragstrip skirmishes, we’re getting 65-mph roll race battles – this time around between a crimson L-bodied Dodge Charger SRT Hellcat packing the iconic 6.2-liter supercharged Hemi V8 and a serious gray R35 Nissan GT-R, with the Godzilla relying on its legendary 3.8-liter VR38DETT twin-turbocharged V6 engine.
Enticed by something else other than the countless prepped surface quarter-mile battles they have witnessed over the years, the videographer keeps showing us that roaring V6 and V8 engines are best witnessed at the highest speed possible – all thanks to the continued high-speed ‘drama’ happening at the legendary Pocono Raceway , a 2.5-mile tri-oval track in Blakeslee, Pennsylvania.
This place has been around sine 1969 and has seen just about everything, including major events like NASCAR, the IndyCar Series, and the IMSA GT Championship series. This time around, we are dealing with one of the smaller gatherings. That doesn’t mean they’re uninteresting, especially RaceMotive’s 65-mph roll race series. So, while we wait for new quarter-mile dragstrip battles, the videographer shows us high-speed clashes between iconic models, like this Hellcat and GT-R .
The protagonists have been presented, so let’s kick off the action with a roaring initial skirmish: both cars felt like they were glued next to each other, and at the end of the first skirmish there was less than one mph between them: 144.88 mph for one of the protagonists and just 145.09 mph for its opponent. The loser quickly asked for a rematch, and it was promptly granted.
So, they went at it again, and they went neck-and-neck all over again. Believe it or not, the separation was once again breathtaking: the winner had a top speed of 152.36 mph while the runner-up posted a 151.33 mph pass! Now, let’s check out the video and find out who’s who!
By the way, the R35 Nissan GT-R has become a relic of the past after production ended last summer. It did have a lengthy run, with manufacturing starting in December 2007 and the grand tourer getting a ton of upgrades over the years, culminating with the GT-R50 that celebrated half a century for the GT-R nameplate.
Meanwhile, the Dodge Charger nameplate is alive and well, offered in eighth-generation form, although fans do miss one thing: the mighty V8. The current STLA Large-based Charger fastback coupe and sedan are only offered as the Daytona with an EV setup or as the Sixpack models featuring the 3.0-liter twin-turbo inline-six Hurricane engine.
